messages:
sanjay: Hey team — after the role refactor landed in private control plane yesterday I just saw an on-prem admin pod spawning a shell into a customer VM (!!!). Not normal.  

sanjay: The change was the `admin` -> `onprem-admin` split, plus a few permissive binds. I think something granted exec privileges to a service account it shouldn't have.

eva: Whoa. Do you have the pod name / service account?

sanjay: pod `cfg-sync-6f7bd` in tenant-prod-42. SA `cfg-sync-sa@tenant-prod`.

mikayla: tagging ops-oncall. Are we seeing it as active exploit or privilege misconfig?

ops-oncall: looking now. Can you paste the exact command you observed?

sanjay: Observed via audit log entry: `exec into pod` with command `/bin/sh -c "curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ iam"` — indicates attempt to reach metadata service. Log excerpt: ```time=1898760000 svc=cplane user=cfg-sync-sa action=exec resource=pod/cfg-sync-6f7bd args=/bin/sh -c curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam```

mikayla: That path would allow token theft if the VM had IMDSv1 enabled. This looks like a lateral move attempt.

dave: Quick checks: 1) revoke `cfg-sync-sa` tokens 2) patch pod to readOnlyRootFilesystem 3) block outbound to 169.254.169.254 at network egress rules for pod netpolicy.

eva: I've rotated the KMS key used for signing cluster tokens and revoking the long-lived SA tokens. Rolling a short policy: `kubectl delete secret cfg-sync-sa-token -n tenant-prod-42`.

audit-bot: Alert created: INC-2026-0423-145. Linked logs: s3://redwood-audit/1898760000/exec-cfg-sync-6f7bd.log

ops-oncall: Applying egress deny to tenant-prod-42 namespace for 169.254.169.254 now.

mikayla: We need to reproduce whether the RBAC role binding change allowed `pods/exec` on that SA. Can someone grep the rolebindings? Suggested query: ```kubectl get rolebindings --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.subjects[]?.name=="cfg-sync-sa")'```

sanjay: Running locally, found rolebinding `rb-onprem-cfgsync` bound to `cfg-sync-sa` with clusterrole `onprem-admin-exec` (new). That clusterrole contains `verbs: ["exec","get","list"]` on `pods/exec` — looks wrong.

eva: Oof. That clusterrole should not exist. Which PR introduced `onprem-admin-exec`?

mikayla: PR #8427 by infra-refactor, merged 1898739000. The role was added as a convenience for platform tasks but accidentally included wildcard pod exec.

dave: Action items: 1) remove `onprem-admin-exec` permission immediately 2) revoke any tokens bound to the SA (eva did); 3) run audit query for `pods/exec` in last 24h across tenants 4) add regression test to prevent `exec` in onprem roles without explicit justification.

eva: I'm rolling back the role to the pre-refactor version and issuing a hotfix to the playbook. Pushing now.

ops-oncall: Confirmed network egress deny in place. I also applied a temporary pod security policy to disallow `hostNetwork: true` and prevent privilege escalation for the affected namespace.

mikayla: Forensics note — capture of the pod filesystem + logs already archived to forensics bucket: s3://redwood-forensics/1898760000/cfg-sync-6f7bd.tar.gz

sanjay: Thanks. Also worth checking if private control plane agents accepted the new role due to incorrect role mapping logic from the control plane -> tenant translation layer. That mapping code was touched in the refactor.

dave: I'll add a test that verifies role equivalence round-trip: controlplane role -> tenant binding -> effective perms.

eva: We should also add an integration gate: PRs that modify clusterroles must include a one-line security justification and a reviewer from eng-security. I'll file a policy change.

ops-oncall: Severity set to P1 until we confirm no other SAs abused. I've notified customer-success for impacted customers in tenant-prod-42.

mikayla: Final ask: create an audit alert for any `exec` into pods from SAs that don't have `exec` explicitly listed in their approved role allowlist. Simple rule: exec must be in an allowlist file tracked in repo.

sanjay: Agree. I'll open the follow-up tickets and add owners. Thanks for the quick responses :thumbsup:

audit-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423-145 updated: mitigations applied, evidence collected, follow-ups assigned.
